newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Cambior's Argentine copper study imminent.
newsitem.headline: Cambior's Argentine copper study imminent.

text.p: The results of a feasibility study of the big Pachon copper project on Argentina's border with Chile should be ready in the second quarter, an official of Canada's Cambior Inc said.
"It's due in the second quarter of this year so it's imminent now," Pachon's Project Manager Richard le Clerc told Reuters in an interview.

The study takes into account an increase of ore throughput at the high altitude site to 100,000 tonnes a day, and preliminary results point to higher output than the 150,000 tonnnes a year of copper in concentrates foreseen earlier.
"I would say we are on the higher side of that (150,000 tonnes a year output) now," le Clerc said.

Once the project's owners -- Cambior has 50 percent and Bolivia's Minera San Jose has the rest -- have approved the study and decided on financing, Pachon's construction should take about three years.

Pachon's ore must be mined quickly, with a big daily throughput, because its porphyry-type copper deposit's lowish grade would make a smaller operation unprofitable. But the ore body has its advantages, including a low stripping ratio and a high grade zone near the top which will be exploited in the first year of operation.
"The other thing which is interesting about Pachon is its potential. It's open at depth and we believe there is more than we have estimated so far," le Clerc said.

Cambior announced in January that it was upgrading its estimate of proven and probable reserves at Pachon to 882 million tonnes graded at 0.62 percent with a 0.4 percent cut-off. The deposit also contains 0.015 percent molybdenum, together with some silver and gold.

The site, at 11,900 feet (3,600 m) above sea level in the Andes mountains, is much closer to Chile's Pacific coast than the Argentine Atlantic, so the concentrates will be shipped from a Chilean port.
"We have a lot of possibilities. We could use Ventanas, which is already a copper concentrates port, and we also have the possibility around Coquimbo," said le Clerc.
Another possibility would be a joint-venture with the nearby Los Pelambres mine in Chile, controlled by Chile's Luksic group, with which Cambior has discussed sharing infrastructure.
"If Pelambres builds a port and we can use it, that's fine, but there's nothing agreed at this time," le Clerc said.
The mine is 20 miles (30 km) from an existing road.
In one of the first agreements of its kind in the region, Argentine and Chile signed a special protocol to allow the mine to operate on both sides of the border in January.
Cambior said in 1995 that Pachon would cost $400 million to $500 million to develop to produce 110,000 tonnes of concentrates a year.
Minera San Jose is 33.3-percent owned by Anglo-Australian mining giant RTZ-CRA. The rest belongs to Andean Resources SA, controlled by the family of Bolivian President Gonzalo Sanchez de Lozada.
Cambior bought 40 percent of Pachon from San Jose in 1994 for $10 million, and acquired another 10 percent after exercising an option to fund exploration and development spending for $5 million.
